land.text: the lands of Henry II of Navarre as count of Foix (Foix, Béarn, Bigorre and Albret), which pass to his daughter Jeanne III and her husband Antoine de Bourbon on 25 May 1555; Cliopatria's House of Bourbon shape of 1556 contains the Foix cells. The crown of Navarre (Lower Navarre) passes in the same succession and is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre.

successors.note: The county of Foix itself lasted to 1607 (Henry IV united Foix, Bigorre, Quatre-Vallées and Nébouzan with the French crown in 1607 (County of Foix page)); the Cliopatria row, and this dossier, stop at the death of Henry II.

capitals.name: Foix
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Foix. Bernard-Roger page: Bernard Roger (count of Couserans, lord of parts of Foix and father of the first count) 'built the square tower of the castle at Foix in France and made it his capital, from which a town grew'.

capitals.name: Orthez
capitals.note: My reading: from the 1290 acquisition of Béarn (the counts' 'main domain') the court sat at Orthez ('Orthez ... from the second half of the 13th century' is the capital of Béarn; Gaston III held court at the Château Moncade in Orthez (Gaston III page)); the county's infobox capital stays Foix and Gaston III stayed at Mazères/Pamiers/Foix when in Foix.

capitals.name: Pau
capitals.note: 'transferring his court from Orthez to Pau in 1464' (Béarn page); the page does not name the count in that sentence.

correction.text: The Foix-proper shape of 1236 carried back to the founding: Roger of Foix inherited 'the town of Foix and the adjoining lands', which had been part of the county of Carcassonne (the Ariège). The pages give no outline for 1034-1235.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1034-1235 (the county begins in the mid-11th century, Cliopatria's first shape in 1236). The 1236 outline (4,586 km2, one Andorran cell that predates the 1278 paréage) is the only extent the record offers, so it is carried back unchanged; the rendering agent should draw it soft. Placed on Roger of Foix (died ca. 1064), 'the title of count of Foix was first assumed by' him (County of Foix page).

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn 1236-1289 only: the county of Foix before the Béarn inheritance of May 1290

keyframe_review.note: 4,586 km2 for Foix proper (Ariège and a few cells of Haute-Garonne and Gers; one Andorran cell). Infobox: 2,466 km2 'just before the French Revolution' (ratio 1.86, inside the factor of two; the infobox is the 18th-century county). The pages do not date 1236 itself. The shape is right for 1236-1289 only: 'In 1290 the counts of Foix acquired the viscountcy Béarn', which Cliopatria adds in 1294. The Andorran cell predates the 8 September 1278 paréage (RB3 page).

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn from 1290 (Béarn and Nébouzan inherited in May 1290) to 1332

keyframe_review.note: 8,813 km2: Foix plus the Pyrénées-Atlantiques cells (Béarn) and the Nébouzan cells. 'when he died in 1290, Roger-Bernard immediately took possession of his counties (May)'; County of Foix page: 'In 1290 the counts of Foix acquired the viscountcy Béarn' and inherited Nébouzan the same year. Cliopatria starts the shape four years late; the shape is unchanged and holds from 1290.
8,766 km2, a re-digitisation of the 1294 shape. Nothing on the pages changes the land 1333-1343; Gaston II reigns to 1343 and Gaston III succeeds him (County of Foix page).

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn 1344-1378: Foix, Béarn and Nébouzan under Gaston III

keyframe_review.note: 8,813 km2 for 1344-1384; right for 1344-1378. Gaston III also held Marsan and Gabardan (on 14 January 1364 at Agen he paid homage to the Black Prince for lands 'inside the Principality of Aquitaine', saying his homage covered only Marsan and Gabardan; Gaston III page), which are Landes lands not in the shape and not dated on any page opened; the Cliopatria shape is kept without them. From 1379 the page adds the Bigorre communities and the western Nébouzan castellanies (new keyframe 1379). Second look: the Gaston III page gives no acquisition date for Marsan and Gabardan (only the homage of January 1364 at Agen) and does not mention Castelbon; the Gaston IV page lists Marsan and Castelbon among his viscounties without dates; the County of Foix page has Matthew of Castelbon count 1391-1398 and 'Archambault of Grailly seized his lands' in 1398. The gazetteer has no Marsan, Gabardan or Castelbon, so they are neither dated nor drawn.

correction.text: The 1344 shape of Foix, Béarn and Nébouzan plus Bigorre (the Hautes-Pyrénées), ceded by its communities to Gaston III in 1379 and given up under the Treaty of Toulouse in January 1390

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1379-1389. '26 conventions were signed between Fébus and Bigorrian communities, and Tarbes was the last to cede on 27 November 1379'; the 3 April 1379 agreement at Barcelonne-du-Gers gave him the Mauvezin and Goudon castellanies, which 'extended Nébouzan westward'. On 5 January 1390 Bigorre was ceded to France for a life annuity (Treaty of Toulouse). Cliopatria draws Bigorre only from 1407; the Béarn dossier (county-of-bearn) draws it from 1379 too.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn 1390-1406: Foix, Béarn and Nébouzan under Matthew of Foix-Castelbon and Archambault of Grailly

keyframe_review.note: 8,766 km2 for 1385-1406; right for 1390-1406 without Bigorre (the 1379-1389 span is the new keyframe above). 'Charles VI ... obtained Foix and Béarn' in 1391, granted the county to Matthew of Foix-Castelbon, and Archambault of Grailly seized it in 1398 and was confirmed in 1401: the land does not change.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn 1407-1446: Foix, Béarn, Nébouzan and Bigorre

keyframe_review.note: 11,061 km2: adds the Hautes-Pyrénées (Bigorre, 10 of 20 cells). 'In 1407, it belonged to Bernard VII of Armagnac, who sold it that year to John I, Count of Foix.' Right for 1407-1446; the Narbonne cells of the next shape belong to 1447.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn from 1447 to 1452: the Foix-Béarn-Bigorre lands plus the viscounty of Narbonne

keyframe_review.note: 12,642 km2: adds cells in Aude and Hérault, the viscounty of Narbonne. 'Gaston IV bought the viscounty of Narbonne' in 1447 (County of Foix page; Gaston IV page 'From 1447, he was also Viscount of Narbonne'). Cliopatria starts the shape three years late; unchanged and holds 1447-1452.

16,425 km2 (the csv figure; 17,450 km2 by the gazetteer's cell count): against 1450 the shape adds 17 cells (about 4,300 km2): Haute-Garonne 7, Hautes-Pyrénées 7, Gers 1, Ariège 1 and one other, at 0.27 E to 0.93 E and 42.79 N to 43.38 N, the Comminges-Nébouzan country and the east of Bigorre. unverified: page silent. Second look at the Gaston IV, Gaston III, County of Foix and County of Comminges pages: none dates a Foix acquisition in 1453. Gaston IV is 'Count of Foix and Bigorre in France from 1436 to 1472' and held 'the viscounties of Marsan, Castelbon, Nébouzan, Villemeur and Lautrec' (Gaston IV page, undated). The Comminges page says 'In 1462, the king of France Louis XI detached the county of Comminges from the royal domain and gave it to his friend' and lists Jean of Foix-Lautrec as count of Comminges 1472-1494 beside two other holders for the same years, so the cells may be Cliopatria's reading of Comminges as Foix land, which no page confirms.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn 1463-1478: Foix, Béarn, Nébouzan, Bigorre and Narbonne under Gaston IV and his successors

keyframe_review.note: 16,402 km2, practically the 1453 shape. Right for 1463-1478. unverified: page budget for what changed in 1463 (the pages are silent). From 1479 the same rulers also hold the crown of Navarre, a personal union that this dossier does not draw (next keyframe).

minus.text: Navarra (Upper Navarre), held by the same rulers in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre

correction.text: The Foix-Béarn lands of 1463-1478 unchanged for 1479-1483. Francis Phoebus (1479) and his sister Catherine (1483) also hold the crown of Navarre, but as a personal union: the kingdom is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre (its keyframe 1463-1511), so the Navarra cells are subtracted here (none are in the 1463 shape).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1479-1483, repaired after review. Not a gain of Navarre: kingdom-of-navarre records 1479 as a rename and keeps Navarre in 1463-1511, so drawing it here would colour the 33 Navarra cells twice. Kingdom of Navarre page: Eleanor 'succeeded him for only 15 days and then died; she left the crown to her grandson, Francis Phoebus', and Catherine I 'succeeded her brother Francis Phoebus in accordance with his will (1483)'; Eleanor was 'Countess of Foix and Béarn' in 1461, and 'Lower Navarre, along with the neighbouring Viscounty of Béarn, survived as an independent kingdom which passed by inheritance'. The page does not use the words personal union for Foix (it uses them only for France 1285-1328 and 1589); that reading is mine. Cliopatria adds Navarre only in 1482.

minus.text: Navarra (Upper Navarre), held by the same rulers in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre

correction.text: Unchanged shape minus the Navarra cells, to be drawn 1484-1491: the Foix and Béarn lands joined to the Albret lands (Périgord, Limoges, Albret) by the marriage of Jean d'Albret and Catherine of Foix. The crown of Navarre they also hold is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre.

keyframe_review.note: 44,913 km2 as drawn by Cliopatria, about 38,950 km2 (154 of 187 cells) once the 33 Navarra cells are removed. The remainder is Foix, Béarn and the Albret lands: Dordogne, Corrèze, Haute-Vienne, Lot-et-Garonne and Lot cells, the Albret lordship and the County of Périgord and Viscounty of Limoges ('In 1470, they inherited the County of Périgord and the Viscounty of Limoges'; Jean of Albret 'became King of Navarre by his marriage with Catherine of Foix ... in 1484' and 'They took possession of the county of Foix'). So the composite of Foix, Béarn and Albret is right from 1484, not from 1482.
45,074 km2 as drawn by Cliopatria, the 1482 shape with a few Haute-Vienne cells added (the pages do not date that); about 38,950 km2 after the 33 Navarra cells are removed. unverified: page budget.

minus.text: Navarra (Upper Navarre), held by the same rulers in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre

correction.text: Unchanged shape minus the Navarra cells (Navarre is held in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre): Foix, Béarn, Albret, Périgord and Narbonne.

keyframe_review.note: 45,144 km2 as drawn by Cliopatria, its largest shape; about 38,950 km2 after the 33 Navarra cells are removed. Catherine and John III were crowned at Pamplona in January 1494 (Navarre page), a Navarre event that this dossier does not draw. The pages date no border change in 1497; John of Foix, viscount of Narbonne, 'renounced his claim' to Navarre in 1497 (County of Foix page), which moved no Foix land.

minus.text: Navarra (Upper Navarre), held by the same rulers in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre

correction.text: Unchanged shape minus the Navarra cells (Navarre is held in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre): Foix, Béarn, Albret, Périgord and Narbonne.

minus.text: Navarra (Upper Navarre), held by the same rulers in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre

correction.text: Unchanged shape minus the Navarra cells, to be drawn 1502-1506: Béarn, Foix, Albret and Narbonne (Navarre is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre).

keyframe_review.note: 41,076 km2 as drawn by Cliopatria, about 33,890 km2 (134 of 167 cells) once the Navarra cells are removed. Against 1497 the shape loses 20 cells (about 5,060 km2): Haute-Garonne 7, Hautes-Pyrénées 8, Gers 2, Ariège 2 and one other (the Comminges-Nébouzan country and the east of Bigorre). Second look at 1502: no page dates a Foix loss in 1500-1507. The nearest dated event is the County of Comminges page: 'in 1498, king Louis XII of France definitely reunited the county of Comminges to the French crown', but the page does not say the counts of Foix held Comminges. The Bigorre page says only that Bigorre went to the crown 'in an exchange of properties' (no year), while the County of Foix page has Henry IV uniting Foix, Bigorre and Nébouzan with the crown in 1607, so the loss of half of Bigorre is unexplained and may be Cliopatria's. The succession dispute with the Narbonne branch ended in 1497 and concerned Navarre (County of Foix and John of Foix pages); the Gaston of Foix (Nemours) page is silent on 1500-1507. Right in its southern-French extent only to 1506 because the Narbonne cells go in 1507 (Gaston exchanged the viscounty of Narbonne for the duchy of Nemours with Louis XII, County of Foix page). unverified: page silent.

union.text: Navarra (Upper Navarre), held by the same rulers in personal union and drawn by kingdom-of-navarre

correction.text: The 1502 shape minus the viscounty of Narbonne, exchanged in 1507 with Louis XII for the duchy of Nemours, and minus the Navarra cells (Navarre is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1507-1511: the 1502 shape without the Narbonne cells (the Aude and Hérault cells that the 1512 shape also lacks) and without the Navarra cells (about 32,370 km2). The Nemours duchy received in exchange lies outside the Cliopatria extent and is not drawn.

30,602 km2: Upper Navarre is gone from the Cliopatria shape, as it already is in this dossier's 1479-1511 shapes. On 18 July 1512 Fadrique de Toledo was sent to invade Navarre and Pamplona, Estella, Olite, Sangüesa and Tudela had fallen by September (Navarre page); that conquest is kingdom-of-navarre's event. Henry II page: 'a small territory north of the Pyrenees mountains by the Spanish conquest of 1512'. The Navarre page says the kingdom was 'annexed by the Courts of Castile to the Crown of Castile in 1515'. Overlap to settle: 3 cells of this shape (about 760 km2, 1.23 W to 0.9 W, 43.08 N to 43.2 N, east Lower Navarre and the Soule side) lie within 30 km of Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, the disk kingdom-of-navarre uses for Lower Navarre 1512-1620.
30,507 km2, the same land; 'two more attempts at liberation in 1516 and 1521' (Navarre page) did not hold ground in 1516.

30,317 km2. Henry II's army 'conquered Pamplona in May 1521, but were ultimately repelled by Charles after the Battle of Noain in June 1521': a Navarre campaign of a few weeks, not a lasting change, and not drawn here (kingdom-of-navarre records the 1521 events; the Foix ledger keeps none).

30,507 km2. In 1530 Charles V evacuated Lower Navarre, 'allowing Henry to seize it' (Henry II page); the extra cells are not visible in the shape (Pyrénées-Atlantiques stays at 19 cells), so the 1530 seizure is not a Foix event here: Lower Navarre is kingdom-of-navarre's land (the event is kept in the notes).
30,484 km2. Henry II 'was created Duke of Albret and a peer of France in 1550' (Albret page), a title, not new land.
30,484 km2 to 1555. 'He died at Hagetmau on 24 May 1555'; successor 'Jeanne III and Antoine' (Henry II page); the Cliopatria House of Bourbon shape from 1556 contains these cells.

region.text: Foix and the adjoining lands that had been part of the county of Carcassonne (the Ariège); the Cliopatria shape of 1236 also holds a few cells of Haute-Garonne and Gers

ledger.note: c. 1034: the county of Foix begins on the Ariège lands detached from the county of Carcassonne. 'The title of count of Foix was first assumed by Roger of Foix (died ca. 1064)', who inherited 'the town of Foix and the adjoining lands'; the infobox dates the county to the 'Mid-11th Century'. The List of counts of Foix (second page; the fetch returned its reign spans without names) has Bernard Roger, 'lord of Foix', 1010-1034 and a next row 1034-1064 that ends where Roger of Foix died, but the Bernard-Roger page dates Bernard Roger's death c. 1024, so 1034 is the list's year and not a page-dated founding.

region.text: Andorra, shared between the count of Foix and the bishop of Urgell

ledger.note: 8 September 1278: Roger-Bernard III and the Bishop of Urgell conclude the paréage that makes the counts of Foix co-princes of Andorra. 'On 8 September 1278, after long negotiations, the count and the bishop concluded a paréage'; County of Foix page: 'From 1278 the counts of Foix, and their legal successors, have also been Co-princes of Andorra.' Cliopatria's 1236 shape already holds one Andorran cell.

region.text: Nébouzan, around Saint-Gaudens in the upper Garonne

ledger.note: 1290: Roger-Bernard III also inherits Nébouzan. Roger Bernard III also inherited Nébouzan from his father-in-law that year (County of Foix page).

1290: the court moves west to Orthez, the capital of Béarn. 'Orthez (from the second half of the 13th century)' is the capital of Béarn; the County of Foix page says Béarn 'became their main domain'. The move itself is not dated by a page: my reading.

region.text: the viscounty of Béarn, which became the counts' main domain; the gazetteer's Béarn is all of Pyrénées-Atlantiques, wider than the viscounty

ledger.note: May 1290: Roger-Bernard III takes Béarn. 'when he died in 1290, Roger-Bernard immediately took possession of his counties (May)' on the death of the man whose Béarn lands came with his wife Margaret of Béarn (married 1252); County of Foix page: 'In 1290 the counts of Foix acquired the viscountcy Béarn', which became their main domain. Inheritance through his wife Margaret of Béarn, not conquest. [Reviewer eu-10-g: counterpart was county-of-bearn, whose dossier starts in 1347; the Roger-Bernard III and County of Foix pages give the inheritance from his father-in-law Gaston VII of Béarn.]

region.text: the castellanies of Mauvezin and Goudon, extending Nébouzan westward

ledger.note: 1379: the western Nébouzan castellanies. After the Count of Comminges died on 15 October 1375 Gaston pursued the inheritance through his mother; the final agreement at Barcelonne-du-Gers on 3 April 1379 gave him the Mauvezin and Goudon castellanies, 'which extended Nébouzan westward'.

region.text: Bigorre, ceded by its communities through 26 conventions, Tarbes last

ledger.note: 27 November 1379: Bigorre cedes to Gaston III. '26 conventions were signed between Fébus and Bigorrian communities, and Tarbes was the last to cede on 27 November 1379'; the 1360 Treaty of Brétigny had 'compensated Fébus for the loss of Bigorre with a cash payout of 200,000 guilders'. The page does not name the previous overlord, so the counterpart is the communities, as in the Béarn dossier.

region.text: Bigorre, the temporary cession of the Treaty of Toulouse

ledger.note: 5 January 1390: Gaston III gives Bigorre up. The Treaty of Toulouse 'incorporated the feudal inheritance of the South into France in exchange for gold payment and the temporary cession of Bigorre'; he received 'a life annuity for Bigorre along with 100,000 francs' and made Charles VI his universal legatee.

1391: Gaston III dies without a legitimate heir and the line passes to Matthew of Foix-Castelbon. 'Febus died on 1 August 1391'; on 20 December 1391 Charles VI annulled the Treaty of Toulouse and recognised Matthew as Gaston's sole heir (County of Foix page: Charles granted the county to Matthew, Viscount of Castelbon). Same state, same colour.

1398: Archambault of Grailly takes Foix. Matthew died without issue and Archambault of Grailly seized his lands (County of Foix page); he was confirmed as count in 1401. The county passes to the Foix-Grailly line; the land does not change.
1407: John I of Foix buys Bigorre. 'In 1407, it belonged to Bernard VII of Armagnac, who sold it that year to John I, Count of Foix. From then on it is a subsidiary title of the counts of Foix.'
1447: Gaston IV buys Narbonne. Gaston IV bought the viscounty of Narbonne (County of Foix page). Cliopatria's shape adds the Narbonne cells from 1450.
1464: the court moves from Orthez to Pau. 'transferring his court from Orthez to Pau in 1464' (the page's sentence does not name the count; Gaston IV was count 1436-1472).

1484: the Albret line joins the Foix inheritance. Jean I of Albret gained the Navarrese crown through his marriage to Catherine of Foix, dated 'Queen of Navarre in 1484'; Henry II of Albret is count of Foix from 1517. Same state, same colour.

region.text: the County of Périgord and the Viscounty of Limoges

ledger.note: 1484: the Périgord and Limousin lands of the Albret line join the composite. House of Albret page: 'In 1470, they inherited the County of Périgord and the Viscounty of Limoges', so the land was the Albret family's from 1470, and Jean of Albret 'became King of Navarre by his marriage with Catherine of Foix ... in 1484' and 'They took possession of the county of Foix'. The counterpart is the Albret line, not county-of-perigord (corrected on review: that dossier ends in 1481 with a dissolve into Foix, three years early and to the wrong heir; its group should move its successor to the Albret, 1470). Cliopatria ends its Périgord row in 1481 and puts the Dordogne, Corrèze and Haute-Vienne cells in this shape from 1482.

region.text: the lordship of Albret around Nérac, with Cliopatria's neighbouring Lot and Gironde cells

ledger.note: 1484: the Albret lordship joins the composite (Lot-et-Garonne and the Gironde and Lot cells of the Cliopatria shape). The Albret page lists the lords of Albret but gives no territory; the extent is the Cliopatria shape's. Same counterpart as the Périgord and Limousin event of the same year: both lands come with the Albret house.

1507: Gaston de Foix gives Narbonne to Louis XII. Gaston de Foix exchanged the viscounty of Narbonne for the duchy of Nemours with Louis XII (County of Foix page). The Nemours duchy is far north of the Cliopatria extent and is not drawn.

region.text: the lands of Henry II of Navarre as count of Foix: Foix, Béarn, Bigorre and Albret

ledger.note: 25 May 1555: Henry II of Navarre dies and his lands pass to Jeanne III and Antoine de Bourbon. Infobox 'Count of Foix 1517 - 25 May 1555'; 'He died at Hagetmau on 24 May 1555'; 'Successor: Jeanne III and Antoine'. The Foix title survives to 1607; the Cliopatria row ends here and its cells are in the House of Bourbon shape of 1556. His crown of Navarre (Lower Navarre) passes in the same succession and is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre. The Henry II page lists the Foix title only; Bigorre and Albret rest on the House of Albret page, which lists 'Béarn, Foix, Bigorre' among the family's possessions without a date.

wars.name: Revolt of the count of Foix against Philip III
wars.outcome: The king besieged Foix on 3 June; the conflict was resolved on 8 February 1273 and the count, released, did homage to the king of France before the end of the year. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The page gives the siege date without the year (placed in 1272 by the surrounding text) and does not say which side Aragon fought on.

wars.name: Revolt of Roger-Bernard III against Peter of Aragon
wars.outcome: Roger-Bernard rose in open rebellion in spring 1280, surrendered on 22 July and was imprisoned until December 1283, freed 'in exchange for the viscounty of Castelbon'. The Castelbon lands are not in the Cliopatria shape.
wars.note: The page's wording on who gave up Castelbon is ambiguous.

wars.name: Foix-Armagnac war over Béarn
wars.outcome: In 1293 Gerard V of Armagnac 'contested the usurpation of Béarn and began a long war'; 'This war lasted until 1377.' Gaston III won at Launac on 5 December 1362 and captured the Armagnac leader. Béarn stayed with Foix, so no border moved.
wars.note: Launac (5 December 1362) from the Gaston III page.

wars.name: Treaty of Brétigny settlement for Bigorre
wars.outcome: The treaty of 8 May 1360 left Bigorre to others and Gaston III received 'a cash payout of 200,000 guilders' for its loss.
wars.note: The Bigorre page says only that the treaty 'made it decisively French'; the pages disagree on who held Bigorre afterwards.

wars.name: War of Comminges

zones.text: the Mauvezin and Goudon castellanies extending Nébouzan westward

wars.outcome: The Count of Comminges died on 15 October 1375; after the battle at Cazères-sur-l'Adour in November 1376, the agreement of Barcelonne-du-Gers (3 April 1379) gave Gaston III the Mauvezin and Goudon castellanies.

certainty.note: Seigneurial frontiers between the Pyrenean counties, Béarn, Armagnac and Comminges are approximate, and nothing outlines the county before Cliopatria's 1236 shape; the line of the Pyrenees against Aragon and Navarre is firm, but no datable change of the southern frontier belongs to this state (Upper Navarre is drawn by kingdom-of-navarre). The Andorran paréage (1278) is a treaty but a single cell.

sources.note: Bernard Roger c. 962-c. 1024, built the tower at Foix and made it his capital; his son Roger I of Foix 'the first count of Foix'.

sources.title: County of Comminges
sources.note: 1462 Louis XI grants Comminges away; 1498 Louis XII reunites it with the crown; context for the 1453 and 1502 shape changes.

sources.title: John of Foix, Viscount of Narbonne
sources.note: Claim to Navarre from 1483, ended in Catherine's favour 1497; died 1500; silent on Foix lands.

sources.title: Gaston of Foix, Duke of Nemours
sources.note: Born 10 December 1489, died at Ravenna 11 April 1512; silent on Narbonne, Comminges and Bigorre.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'County of Foix' 1236-1555 is the Foix-Béarn lands to 1478 and, from its 1482 shape, the Albret lands (Périgord, Limousin, Albret) and the 33 cells of Navarra (Upper Navarre) as well. REPAIR OF 2026-10-25, decided in this dossier: Navarre is not drawn by Foix. From 1479 (Francis Phoebus; Catherine 1483; Henry II 1517) the counts of Foix are also kings of Navarre, a personal union in my reading (the Kingdom of Navarre page does not name it so): kingdom-of-navarre records 1479 as a rename, keeps Navarre in its keyframe 1463-1511, and carries the 1512 invasion, the 1521 war, Lower Navarre (lost 1525, retaken 1527) and the end in 1620. So the Navarra cells are subtracted from the shapes of 1479-1511, there is no 1479 gain, and the Navarre events and wars were moved here from the ledger: 1479 Francis Phoebus inherits the crown (Navarre page); 18 July 1512 Fadrique de Toledo's invasion, the towns fallen by September and the loss of Upper Navarre (Navarre page); May 1521 Pamplona retaken and 30 June 1521 defeat at Noáin (Henry II page); 1530 Henry II seizes Lower Navarre after the Treaty of Cambrai (Henry II page); the wars 'Spanish conquest of Upper Navarre' 1512-1515 and 'Navarrese reconquest attempt of 1521'. If the orchestrator would rather have Foix draw Navarre, kingdom-of-navarre must record the 1479 loss and the 1512 events must come back here. Remaining overlap: 3 cells of the Foix shape 1512-1555 (about 760 km2, east Lower Navarre and Soule) lie within 30 km of Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, the disk kingdom-of-navarre draws for Lower Navarre.
Other rows to coordinate: (1) 'County of Béarn' (county-of-bearn, 1347-1555 in its dossier) is read as the eastern Foix lands while this shape holds Béarn proper from 1294, and both dossiers record the 1379, 1390 and 1407 Bigorre events; (2) Cliopatria's County of Périgord ends in 1481 and its dossier dissolves into Foix, but the House of Albret page puts Périgord and Limoges with the Albret from 1470, so the 1484 Périgord/Limousin gain here names the Lordship of Albret and county-of-perigord's group should move its successor to the Albret; (3) the House of Bourbon row takes these cells in 1556.
Start: the pages place the county in the mid-11th century (infobox 'Mid-11th Century'; 'the title of count of Foix was first assumed by Roger of Foix (died ca. 1064)'). The dossier now starts in 1034 (confidence 2), the first year of the List of counts of Foix row that ends in 1064, with the 1236 shape carried back; the Bernard-Roger page dates Bernard Roger's death c. 1024 against the list's 1034. The county lasted to 1607 (Henry IV); the row ends with Henry II in 1555.
Ruler strip: the List of counts of Foix and the House of Foix pages were opened; their tables came back with reign spans (1034-1064, 1064-1071, 1071-1124, 1124-1148, 1148-1188, 1188-1223, 1223-1241, 1241-1265, 1265-1302, 1302-1315, 1315-1343, 1343-1391, 1391-1398, 1398-1428 with 1398-1412, 1412-1436, 1436-1472, 1472-1483, 1483-1517 with 1484-1516, 1517-1555, 1555-1572 with 1555-1562) and no names except Bernard Roger, so no strip is given; a gap-filler with a route to the names can use these spans.
Not explained by any page opened (second look included, 15 pages): the 1453 growth (17 cells in the Comminges-Nébouzan country and east Bigorre), the 1463 re-digitisation, the 1492 Haute-Vienne cells and the 1502 loss of 20 cells (Comminges country and half of Bigorre). The County of Comminges page gives 1462 (Louis XI grants the county away) and 1498 (Louis XII reunites it with the crown) but does not tie Comminges to the counts of Foix; the Bigorre page says only that Bigorre went to the crown 'in an exchange of properties', undated, against the County page's 1607 union of Foix, Bigorre and Nébouzan. Marsan and Gabardan (held by 14 January 1364) and Castelbon are not in the shape and not dated.
The pages disagree on who held Bigorre after 1360: the Gaston III page says Gaston was compensated for its loss at Brétigny, the Bigorre page says Brétigny made it decisively French; the Gaston IV page has him count of Bigorre from 1436.
Region names the gazetteer lacks: Nébouzan. Counterparts without a dossier: County of Comminges; Viscounty of Narbonne; Lordship of Albret; Bishop of Urgell (co-prince of Andorra).
